name: Halverson Synth-Wool Occasion Tuxedo
description:
A single-button tuxedo in a deep charcoal synth-wool blend with a satin-analog lapel that catches light cleanly without looking cheap. Halverson's mid-market tuxedo line is built for the Tier 2-3 customer who attends corporate events, union ceremonies, or the occasional Tier 3 social function and needs to look correctly dressed without spending a month's rent. The jacket features augment-compatible seaming at the shoulders and a discreet port-access panel along the left side, closed with a magnetic seam that lies flush when not in use. The trousers have a single satin-analog stripe down each leg and are cut with enough room in the seat to accommodate minor geneware — standard tail modifications require aftermarket alteration.

It is not a remarkable garment. That is precisely its value. A person wearing this tuxedo registers as appropriately formal and nothing more — no tier signal strong enough to cause friction, no affiliation display to read. For Tier 2 workers attending Tier 3 functions, invisibility is the point.
cultural_context: The default tuxedo of Meridian's working professional class. Rental versions circulate widely through Tier 2 social networks. Owning one rather than renting signals a degree of social ambition. Seen at union investiture ceremonies, corporate welcome events, and Tier 3 weddings.
story_hooks: A character buys this tuxedo specifically for a job interview at a Tier 4 corponation. They are told, gently, that the event is business casual. They wear it anyway.
The augment port panel is a standard feature, but someone has modified theirs to conceal a secondary compartment. Whatever was inside it is gone. The previous rental owner left no other trace.
Two colleagues show up to the same corporate gala in identical Halverson tuxedos. The evening becomes about something other than the event.

physical_description.visual_profile: A conservative single-button tuxedo jacket with a sharp, professional silhouette. The charcoal synth-wool reads as formal without ostentation. The satin-analog lapels catch ambient light with a clean, muted sheen that avoids the cheap gloss of lower-tier formal wear. Worn with matching high-waisted trousers featuring subtle satin-analog side stripes. The overall impression is polished, corporate-adjacent, and deliberately unremarkable — a garment designed to make the wearer invisible within formal contexts.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not fitted. Shoulders cut with augment-accommodation seams that allow for subcutaneous implants or minor geneware without visible bunching. Jacket length falls just below the hip. Trousers have a relaxed, mid-rise cut with enough seat room for standard tail modifications. Movement is unrestricted; the garment prioritizes comfort over drama.
physical_description.primary_material: Synth-wool blend — synthetic fibers engineered to mimic wool's thermal and drape properties without cost or maintenance burden. Satin-analog lapels use a treated microfiber that simulates high-thread silk without the price tag.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, matte weave with a soft nap. Lapels have a subtle luster that catches light without reflectivity. Seaming is clean and professional throughout. No visible distressing or intentional wear.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep charcoal (nearly black, slightly warm). Satin-analog lapels in a fractionally lighter charcoal that creates depth without contrast. White dress shirt standard; tie color left to wearer discretion.
physical_description.closures: Single mother-of-pearl button at jacket front. Magnetic seam panel at left side (for augment port access) lies completely flush when closed. Trousers feature standard friction-fit waistband with concealed hook fastener.
distinctive_features: Augment-compatible seaming at shoulders — designed to accommodate subcutaneous implants without visible strain
Discreet magnetic-seam port-access panel on left jacket side — closes flush and undetectable when not in use
Satin-analog lapels engineered for light-catch without gloss
Satin-analog side stripe on each trouser leg — narrow, functional, status-neutral
Clean interior construction with reinforced seams at stress points
No visible branding or manufacturer insignia
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 aspirational. Signals stable employment and social participation without claiming wealth or status. Rental circulation is common; ownership marks modest upward mobility.
physical_description.cultural_context: The uniform of Meridian's working professional class. Worn at union ceremonies, corporate welcome events, Tier 3 social functions, and occasions requiring formal dress without affiliation statement. The garment's value lies in its invisibility — it allows the wearer to blend into formal spaces without drawing attention or triggering status friction.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new or freshly rented. Worn versions show subtle creasing at elbows and knees, minimal wear at collar and cuffs. No patching or heavy weathering — this is an indoor garment maintained with standard care.

image_prompt: A Tier 2-3 neo-noir professional in a charcoal Halverson synth-wool tuxedo, standing in a dimly lit corporate lobby or union hall. Soft tungsten lighting catches the subtle sheen of the satin-analog lapels. The wearer's posture is composed and professional. Shot at medium distance showing full silhouette. Dark urban background with faint neon glow from distant signage. The garment appears tailored, pressed, and deliberately unremarkable. No visible augmentations. Moody, formal tone. --ar 2:3 --v 6
